messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Hosted API - eu-west-1 high tail latency. Queue growth on hosted-request-queue-1. p95 jumped from ~480ms to ~3.2s, p99 ~1.4s -> 9.8s. GPU pool 'eu-prod-a' reported at 100% utilization; autoscaler hitting max_replicas=60 and failing to provision new instances.
alyssa_oncall: ACK. I'm on it. Linking runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/hosted-queue-growth>
alyssa_oncall: Quick check: metrics query ->
```
sum(rate(hosted.request_queue.length[1m])) by (pool)
```
Result: hosted-request-queue-1 trending +12k/min sustained for last 6m.
sre-ben: Are we seeing cloud provider quota 429s on the provisioner? I saw a few earlier.
alyssa_oncall: Yes - provisioner logs show repeated 429 from infra-api when creating GPUs. Snippet:
```
2026-03-16T22:09:12Z provisioner:error createNode -> 429 QuotaExceeded: request denied
```
infra-raj: Confirmed. Support ticket with cloud: CASE-87432 opened. They're reporting temporary regional NPU/GPU allocation constraint. ETA unknown ~ 30-90m.
eng-maya: If autoscaler can't grow, can we fall back to a lighter model variant for hosted to reduce per-request GPU time? We have redwood-medium-quant ready in eu.
alyssa_oncall: Good idea. Plan A: enable model-fallback routing for non-SLA routes -> switch from redwood-large to redwood-medium-quant. That should cut GPU token time ~45%.
alyssa_oncall: Plan B: enable emergency request-shedding for best-effort customers (rate-limit header + 503 with Retry-After). Preparing curl patch to feature flag.
cs-tom: Customer note: we already have 3 customers reporting errors from EU users (chat feature timeouts). I'll notify them we're investigating and may throttle non-critical traffic.
sre-ben: Rolling the fallback now. Patch:
```
POST /internal/route-flags
{ "route": "hosted.large", "fallback": "redwood-medium-quant", "active": true }
```
sre-ben: Applied. Telemetry: p95 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.6s in ~60s. p99 from 9.8s -> 4.5s and queue length growth slowed.
infra-raj: Cloud case updated: provider extended soft limit but still we cannot create >8 new nodes in next 10m. Manual scale attempts will get throttled.
alyssa_oncall: Because autoscaler can't provision fast enough, I'm increasing local batching in the serving runtime for EU to reduce per-token overhead (patching config):
```
serving.runtime.batch_window_ms = 8 -> 20
```
eng-maya: Watch for latency tail regressions; batching can help throughput but might increase p95 for tiny requests.
alyssa_oncall: Noted. Observing metrics: small increase in average latency but tail is improving overall. Queue delta now near zero.
sre-ben: Opening temporary circuit-breaker for non-authenticated public endpoints to shed 15% traffic gracefully.
cs-tom: Customers updated on status page, sent to affected account owners.
infra-raj: We're still seeing a few 429s to infra API when autoscaler reconciles. Cloud says regional replenishment in 45-75m but not guaranteed.
alyssa_oncall: Handoff to night oncall @sre-ben in 20m with tasks: continue monitoring queue, keep fallback model routing enabled, keep batching window, escalate to cloud if 429s persist after 30m.
sre-ben: ACK takeover. I'll keep the thread updated and will trigger escalation if p99 > 6s for another 5m.
cs-tom: I'll open follow-ups with the three impacted customers and create a post-incident summary draft.
incident-bot: [INFO] Pager duty: responder @sre-ben assigned. Incident severity set to P2 due to customer impact and partial mitigation in place. Logs and runbook pinned to channel.
alyssa_oncall: Leaving notes: actions taken = model-fallback enabled, batching increased, circuit-breaker enabled, cloud case opened. Recommend retrospective on autoscaler max_replicas defaults and cross-region pre-warming.
sre-ben: Taking over — monitoring dashboard -> <https://redwood.internal/dashboards/hosted-eu-queue>
sre-ben: closing handoff. Will escalate if anything regresses. :thumbsup:"
